title: "Adapter"
description: "A small trainable module added to a pretrained model to adapt it to a task."
term: "Adapter"
letter: "A"
category: "LLM Engineering"
difficulty: "Intermediate"

## Simple explanation

An adapter is a small set of trainable components placed inside or alongside
a pretrained model. Instead of changing every model weight for a new task,
training updates the adapter while the main model stays fixed.

## Technical explanation

In parameter-efficient fine-tuning, adapter modules add a relatively small
number of parameters to a frozen backbone. A common design uses a
down-projection, a non-linearity, and an up-projection, with a residual
connection. Adapter designs vary, and the term can also refer more broadly
to modules that connect components with different interfaces.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Adapters can reduce the trainable parameter count and make it practical to
maintain task- or domain-specific model variants. They still require
evaluation, compatibility management, and inference resources.

## How it works

The pretrained model computes its usual representation. An adapter
transforms that representation, and its result is combined with the original
through a residual path. During training, gradients update adapter
parameters while the backbone weights are frozen.

## Practical example

A team can keep one frozen language model and train separate adapters for
distinct internal text-classification tasks, selecting the matching adapter
at inference time.

## Common misconceptions

- Adapters do not eliminate the cost of storing or running the base model.
- Adapter weights are generally tied to a compatible base-model
  configuration.
- Adapters are one parameter-efficient tuning approach, not a synonym for all
  fine-tuning.
